evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00739-001 啚; relationship and historical interpretations
evidence.text: The dictionary records 啚 as a variant/use for 圖, but reports conflicting older accounts: Duan Yucai reads the Shuowen component as conveying care or difficulty; the Five Classics Characters text and later dictionaries object to using 啚 for 圖. The editors conclude that the use is attested and include it as a variant. This does not establish 啚’s original role in 圖.
evidence.title: [A00739] 圖 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry states that 圖 had cursive abbreviated forms, including a cited form from Wang Xianzhi; it says the shape was further simplified to 图 and standardized in the mainland simplified-character list. It supports 圖 → 图 as simplified_form, but does not date the cursive abbreviation or specify a first date for standardization.

evidence.field: A00739形體資料表; early witnesses and availability
evidence.text: The entry indexes a Shuowen seal-form witness and variant references, but marks its oracle-bone, bronze-inscription, and several paleographic reference collections unavailable in the online interface. Its editorial notes report Han clerical forms cited from named steles. No directly inspectable early inscription image was available in this research session.

gaps: No usable direct image URL with clear reuse permission and verifiable identity for a historical 圖 glyph was found. The Ministry entry includes a Shuowen witness but gives no clear glyph-image reuse grant; Xiaoxuetang rights are clear but its character-specific result did not load; exact 圖 Commons searches produced no matching file. No glyph is proposed.

The inspected Ministry source documents disputed interpretations of 啚 and the simplified shape’s cursive route, but does not establish an original map pictograph or settle whether 啚 contributed semantically, phonetically, or both.

No independently dated sequence connecting ancient graphic forms to modern 圖 was established. The source indexes Han stele forms but online access to several inscription reference collections is unavailable.

Semantic chronology remains unresolved: this research pass did not establish dated earliest attestations for map, picture, territory, planning, or seeking senses. The dossier’s Zhouli passage is textual evidence but does not independently date the wording.

limitations.text: No image candidate met both identity/provenance and reuse-rights requirements after searching Commons and the Xiaoxuetang query interface and inspecting Ministry reuse information. A visible Ministry Shuowen witness could not be selected because no glyph-image reuse permission was established; Xiaoxuetang’s CC0 permission could not be paired with an accessible 圖 record.
